cards.title: Fresh Riyadh airport attack claim widens the Red Sea risk
cards.summary: AP reported explosions and a Houthi claim around Riyadh’s airport on Thursday as Saudi-backed forces press an offensive near the Bab el-Mandeb.
detail: The Associated Press reported several explosions in Riyadh on Thursday, including a large blast heard near King Khalid International Airport. The Houthis claimed responsibility and said a ballistic missile caused damage, but AP said the claim was not independently evidenced at publication time.

The report follows Saudi authorities’ account of earlier attacks that killed three people at Riyadh and Abha airports. Reuters reporting likewise described the airport strikes and a broader Saudi-backed counteroffensive against Houthi-held positions near the Bab el-Mandeb.

The practical stakes are civilian aviation, oil-facility security, shipping insurance, and humanitarian access through a strategic Red Sea gateway. The geography connects the local fighting to a wider disruption risk without proving a durable change in control.

The next checks are airport operations, independent damage assessment, shipping advisories, and whether the reported Saudi-backed advance holds. Houthi operational claims and the full damage picture remain attributed rather than settled facts.

cards.summary: AP reports that a major-disaster declaration has authorized direct assistance in seven Ohio counties while relief funding is being folded into campaign messaging.

The next check is which counties receive applications, inspections and payments, and whether additional requests are approved. Ohio’s official emergency-management channels remain the primary source for resident instructions.

cards.title: U.S. freezes Microsoft and other firms out of PERM green-card programme
cards.summary: The administration suspended Microsoft, Adobe and major IT outsourcers from a labor-certification route for employment-based green cards, citing alleged fraud and worker-protection concerns.
detail: The Associated Press and Reuters reported that the administration suspended Microsoft, Adobe, and several major IT outsourcing firms from the Department of Labor’s Permanent Labor Certification Program, known as PERM. Officials said the move was tied to allegations of fraud and claims that companies should hire more U.S. workers.

PERM is a labor-certification step used in many employment-based green-card cases; the action is therefore broader than a change to H-1B visa validity itself. Reuters reported that nine universities were also opened to investigation in the same announcement.

The policy matters for technology employers, foreign workers, and universities that depend on international talent. It also creates a test of whether the administration’s enforcement theory survives company responses, agency process, and possible litigation.

The key uncertainty is scope: the public statements describe a suspension and investigations, but the duration, affected filings, and legal challenge path require formal agency notices and company responses.

cards.title: Alito warns the Supreme Court cannot absorb the emergency-appeal surge
cards.summary: Justice Samuel Alito says the volume of emergency applications has risen sharply as executive actions generate fast-moving litigation.
detail: The Associated Press reported that Justice Samuel Alito said the Supreme Court has little ability to reverse the rise in emergency appeals. The court is now handling a volume of urgent applications that, according to Alito’s account, rivals the number of cases it hears with full briefing and argument.

That matters because emergency orders can decide policy while a case is still developing, especially when executive actions are challenged before lower-court proceedings finish. Alito’s comments are a warning about institutional load, not a ruling on any particular dispute.

The official October term calendar shows the court hearing Department of Air Force v. Prutehi Guahan on Oct. 7, alongside a term agenda that includes climate change, immigration and gun-rights cases. The schedule establishes what is before the court; it does not predict outcomes.

The next signal is whether the justices use ordinary merits review, emergency orders or procedural rulings to manage the docket. The volume and pace are documented; the long-term effect on doctrine and public confidence remains open.

cards.summary: The Commission said the EU Civil Protection Mechanism has been activated 10 times for fires this season, which began exceptionally early in late April.

cards.summary: Valencia overturned an early deficit at Casademont Zaragoza, shooting 14 of 21 from three after halftime to start its domestic campaign 1–0.

cards.title: Antonelli wins Monza from 19th as Mercedes finishes one-two
cards.summary: Kimi Antonelli recovered from an engine-penalty start to win the Italian Grand Prix ahead of George Russell and Max Verstappen.
detail: Formula 1’s official result records Kimi Antonelli winning the 53-lap Italian Grand Prix in 1:51:15.281, with George Russell 3.857 seconds back and Max Verstappen third. Antonelli started 19th after an engine penalty and passed his Mercedes teammate late in the race.

The result is a competitive statement because the home driver converted a deep-grid start into a victory while Mercedes secured the top two places. It also changes the championship read more than a routine pole-to-flag win would have done.

F1 reported that a virtual safety car helped Antonelli pit for fresh mediums while Russell stayed on used hard tyres. The official report confirms the result and strategy context; it does not make the next circuit’s tyre picture predictable.
The next race is the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on the published calendar. The open question is whether Antonelli’s Monza pace travels to a very different circuit.
